PLAINTIFE’S RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS TO ECF NO. 96 AND MOTION TO SET
ASIDE OR MODIFY THAT ORDER, DETERMINE REASSIGNMENT AUTHORITY,
AND GRANT LEAVE TO SUPPLEMENT ECF NO. 93

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine objects under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 72(a) and 28
U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A) to the Order entered October 22, 2026 (ECF No. 96). Plaintiff moves to set
aside or modify that Order, to determine the authority under which this action was reassigned and
the procedure by which the successor Magistrate Judge was designated, and for leave under Local
Civil Rule 7(F)(1) to file the supplement to ECF No. 93 attached as Exhibit A. A Memorandum in
Support accompanies this Motion under Local Civil Rules 7(F)(1) and 72. Plaintiff incorporates it
by reference.

I. THE DISPOSITION CHALLENGED

1. The docket for October 22, 2026 records two actions. An unnumbered entry
states: “Case Reassigned to Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick. Magistrate Judge Ivan D.

Davis no longer assigned to the case.” ECF No. 96, signed by Magistrate Judge Davis, addresses

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97_ Filed 10/23/26 Page 2 of 10 PagelD# 978

Plaintiff’?s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis Under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4) and
§ 455(a), and for Priority Determination (ECF No. 86). The docket entry for ECF No. 96 states
that the matter “can be resolved without oral argument,” orders that the Motion “is DENIED AS
MOOT,” and states: “The case has been reassigned to Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick.”

2. The quotations in this Motion and in the Memorandum in Support are taken from
the October 22, 2026 docket entry for ECF No. 96.

3. Both actions are dated October 22, 2026. ECF No. 96 describes the reassignment
as completed. The available entries do not establish the relative timing of execution, issuance,
entry, and the effective termination or modification of the relevant designation.

4. These Objections are directed to ECF No. 96. The administrative reassignment
entry is addressed through the District Judge’s authority over the referral under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)
and Local Civil Rule 72.

IL. TIMELINESS

5. Rule 72(a) requires objections within 14 days after service of the order. ECF No.
96 was entered October 22, 2026. These Objections are filed within 14 days of that date and are
timely under Rule 72(a).

6. These Objections do not extend, restart, or replace any period to object to any
other order. Plaintiff’s pending submissions concerning ECF Nos. 63, 64, 65, and 84 (ECF Nos.
66, 67, 76, 89, 90, 91, 93, 94) remain pending on their own terms. Plaintiff maintains each of them
by this reference.

I. OBJECTIONS
Objection One: Authority to adjudicate ECF No. 86.

7. Predicate. ECF No. 96 states that the case “has been reassigned.” The reassignment

entry states that Magistrate Judge Davis is “no longer assigned to the case.” The record does not

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97 _ Filed 10/23/26 Page 3 of 10 PagelD# 979

identify the designation under which Magistrate Judge Davis acted on October 22, 2026, the scope
of the reassignment, or any authority retained over ECF No. 86.

8. Ground. A magistrate judge’s authority to hear and determine a pretrial matter
derives from a designation under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A) and Local Civil Rule 72. Plaintiff
objects to the disposition of ECF No. 86 if, when ECF No. 96 was issued, the reassignment had
terminated the authority necessary to adjudicate that motion and no applicable statutory, standing,
or case-specific authority permitted the disposition. Plaintiff requests identification of the
operative authority and the effect of reassignment on it. The objection does not rest merely on the
absence of a separately docketed referral order.

9. Relief. Determination of the operative authority and the effect of the reassignment
on it. If the authority necessary to adjudicate ECF No. 86 had ended and no other authority
permitted the disposition, vacatur of ECF No. 96.

10. This objection does not depend on whether a financial interest in Meta Platforms,
Inc. was held on any date.

Objection Two: Permissible administrative action after recusal or during required
disqualification.

11. Predicate. ECF No. 96 disposes of the whole of ECF No. 86, including the requests
in ECF No. 86, Parts V and VII(A2), for determinations of fact. The record does not state whether
the reassignment reflected a recusal, another disqualification determination, or another
administrative basis.

12. Ground. A judge who has recused takes no action in the case beyond the ministerial
steps needed to transfer it. Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC v. NTE Carolinas I, LLC, No. 22-2168,
slip op. at 52-54 (4th Cir. Aug. 5, 2024) (published), reported at 111 F.4th 337; Arnold v. Eastern

Air Lines, Inc., 712 F.2d 899, 904—05 (4th Cir. 1983) (en banc). The same limit applies during a

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97 _ Filed 10/23/26 Page 4 of 10 PagelD# 980

period in which 28 U.S.C. § 455 requires disqualification. McCuin v. Texas Power & Light Co.,
714 F.2d 1255, 1261 (Sth Cir. 1983); In re BellSouth Corp., 334 F.3d 941, 949-50 & n.4 (11th
Cir. 2003). Plaintiff contends that disposing of ECF No. 86 after the relevant authority ended
would exceed implementation of a transfer. Plaintiff objects to ECF No. 96 to the extent it
constitutes adjudication after an established recusal or during a period in which § 455 required
disqualification.

13. ‘Relief. Determination whether ECF No. 96 was authorized adjudication,
permissible administrative closure, or action beyond the authority remaining. If the latter, vacatur
of ECF No. 96 and independent disposition of ECF No. 86’s prospective request by the District
Judge.

14. The two objections are independent. Each identifies its own predicate, ground,
and relief.

IV. RELATED REQUESTS
A. Request Concerning the Successor Designation and Conditional Corrective
Relief.

15. Plaintiff requests identification of the authority and procedure that produced the
successor designation. If the designation resulted from discretionary selection by a disqualified
officer or another unauthorized process, Plaintiff requests correction under the Court’s governing
assignment procedures, administered without the disqualified officer’s participation. Plaintiff
requests Clerk-administered random selection to the extent authorized by those procedures. If the
existing designation complied with the governing procedure, Plaintiff requests that determination.

16. Plaintiff does not allege that Magistrate Judge Davis selected Magistrate Judge
Fitzpatrick. Plaintiff raises no objection to Magistrate Judge Fitzpatrick personally. Plaintiff does

not seek the reinstatement of Magistrate Judge Davis.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97_ Filed 10/23/26 Page 5 of 10 PagelD# 981

B. Alternative Relief: Define ECF No. 96’s Effect in Determining ECF No. 93.
17. ECF No. 96 disposed of ECF No. 86 on mootness grounds following

reassignment. It did not determine whether the challenged earlier participation complied with 8
455 and did not adjudicate ECF No. 93. Plaintiff requests that the District Judge decide ECF No.
93 on its own grounds, resolving the statutory facts to the extent necessary to that decision, or
granting independently warranted relief without reaching unnecessary questions.

18. Plaintiff does not contend that ECF No. 96 purports to decide ECF No. 93. The
request is for the District Judge to define the effect of ECF No. 96 when adjudicating the pending
retrospective application.

C. Leave to Supplement ECF No. 93.
19. The October 22, 2026 developments postdate ECF No. 93 and bear on the relief it

requests. Plaintiff requests leave under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) to file the Proposed Supplement
attached as Exhibit A, which is confined to those developments and their effect on ECF No. 93 §
10(R1) through (R7), with such opportunity for the Defendants to respond as the Court directs.

V. RELIEF REQUESTED

20. Plaintiff requests an order, in the form of the accompanying Proposed Orders:

(1) granting leave to file Exhibit A;

(2) retaining in the District Judge the determination of the Objections and related
requests, and placing on the record, in the decision itself, through a statement of the Clerk, or from
existing records, the following: the effective scope of the reassignment and, where material and
available, its timing relative to ECF No. 96; whether authority over ECF No. 86 remained and the
source of that authority; whether the reassignment reflected recusal, another disqualification
determination, or another administrative basis relevant to the Objections; and the governing

successor-selection procedure and whether that procedure was followed;

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97 _ Filed 10/23/26 Page 6 of 10 PagelD# 982

(3) affording the parties an opportunity to address any newly supplied material
factual information before it becomes a basis for decision;

(4) upon sustaining Objection One or Objection Two, vacating ECF No. 96 and
disposing independently of ECF No. 86’s prospective request, with the material statutory questions
addressed as necessary in deciding ECF No. 93;

(5) in the alternative, leaving the prospective mootness disposition in place,
identifying its limited effect as stated in paragraph 17, and determining ECF No. 93 on its own
grounds;

(6) identifying the authority and procedure that produced the successor designation
and, if that designation resulted from an unauthorized process, correcting it as stated in paragraph
15;

(7) determining the Objections in coordination with ECF Nos. 66, 67, 76, 89, 90, 91,
93, and 94, distinguishing in the order the relief granted, the requests that remain pending, and the
requests rendered unnecessary by complete relief; and

(8) providing that no relief granted returns any referred matter to Magistrate Judge
Davis.

21. Plaintiff does not contend that the filing of these Objections stays any order or
makes ECF No. 59-1 the operative pleading. Vacatur of ECF No. 96 would not by itself vacate
ECF No. 64 or ECF No. 84 or grant ECF No. 59. Those requests are stated in ECF Nos. 66, 67,
89, 90, 91, 93, and 94 and are determinable on their own grounds.

VI. SUBMISSION
22. Local Civil Rule 72 provides that an objection under Rule 72(a) “shall be

considered a motion and is subject to the briefing and notice requirements on Local Civil Rule 7.”

Plaintiff waives oral argument on this Motion only and requests that the Court direct its submission

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document97 _ Filed 10/23/26 Page 7 of 10 PagelD# 983

on the papers under Local Civil Rules 7(E) and 7(J) and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 78(b). A
Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for Submission on the Papers accompanies this
Motion. The waiver does not withdraw the objections stated in ECF Nos. 66 and 67 to provisions
of ECF Nos. 63 and 65.

23. Plaintiff submits with this Motion: the Memorandum in Support; Exhibit A;
Proposed Orders A, B, and C; and the Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for
Submission on the Papers. Plaintiff relies on the existing record, including ECF Nos. 86 through
94 and their attachments.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter Proposed Order A and,
upon determination of these Objections, Proposed Order B or, in the alternative, Proposed Order
C.
